title: Release Watchtower — cohort snapshots, per-route traces, and rollback orchestration UX
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Build a cohesive Console experience (Release Watchtower) that helps engineers run canary rollouts, A/B tests, and shadow traffic experiments with clear per-route metrics, linked traces, cohort diff visualizations, and a configurable auto-rollback workflow. The goal is to reduce time-to-detect regressions and automate safe rollback while preserving observability for postmortem and tuning.
goals: Provide an at-a-glance dashboard for any rollout that surfaces P50/P90 latency, token throughput, error rate, quality regression signals (custom evals), and cost delta per route/route-group
Enable cohort-to-cohort diffing with statistical significance hints and per-metric effect sizes
Surface sampled request traces with model-level annotations (model version, quantization profile, kernel selection) and links to raw prompts/responses where permitted
Offer a configurable auto-rollback policy editor and an execution log (who/what/when) that integrates with rollouts and dedicated capacity
Support shadow traffic analysis: collect metrics without impacting user traffic and highlight divergence between shadow vs. production cohorts
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard view in Console that accepts a rollout_id and shows per-route P50/P90 latency, error rate, token throughput, and cost delta (mock data acceptable for MVP)
Cohort diff UI that displays baseline vs canary with percent change, confidence interval, and a red/yellow/green health indicator per metric
Trace viewer integration: clicking a significant delta allows drilling to 3 example request traces and shows model annotations
Auto-rollback policy form with threshold conditions (latency/error/quality delta) and a simulated run button that shows what would have triggered rollback in a historical window
Audit log entries created when an auto-rollback triggers or when a manual rollback is executed (user, timestamp, trigger reason)
scope: MVP focuses on Console UI + minimal backend endpoints to fetch pre-aggregated per-route metrics and sampled traces. Full real-time stream ingestion and long-term retention are out of scope for MVP. Integrations with Dedicated autoscaler will be documented but not required for rollout execution in MVP.
tradeoffs: MVP will use pre-aggregated metrics (5m windows) to simplify backend load at cost of finer-grained detection latency
Statistical tests will be conservative (bootstrap CI or Welch's t-test) to reduce false positives; this may delay detection of subtle regressions
Initially restrict trace redaction and prompt visibility to users with audit privileges to reduce compliance scope
decisions: Use 5-minute aggregation windows for per-route dashboards in MVP (deferred: 1m windows for high-sensitivity rollouts)
Health indicator thresholds will be configurable per-project but default to: P90 latency +20% (yellow), +50% (red); error rate absolute +0.5pp (yellow), +1.5pp (red)
Auto-rollback actions for MVP: switch traffic back to previous stable model version; do NOT automatically scale infra or modify routing beyond model switch
tasks: PM: finalize schema for per-route metrics and cohort metadata (PRD link)
Design: deliver mockups for dashboard, diff view, and rollback policy editor (link below)
Eng: implement backend endpoints to serve aggregated metrics and sampled traces
Eng: wire Console frontend components to rollout API and add interactive diff visualizations
Security: run privacy & access review for trace/prompt visibility
QA: run end-to-end smoke tests including simulated auto-rollback scenarios
